difference.teaches: subtraction as difference: comparing two amounts (bars, cubes, number line) and finding how many more or fewer
difference.representation: two cube trains or bars drawn one above the other; write the difference and the number sentence
difference.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

count_start_at.option: start: 20 / 50 (tracks inside 20-50 or 50-100); the same on hundreds_chart_fill (the rows shown start at 20 or 50)
count_start_at.name: Count From 20 or 50 (option)
count_start_at.teaches: continue a number track (or fill a hundred-square window) that stays inside 20-50, or inside 50-100
count_start_at.representation: the skill's own track or chart window, numbers held to the step's span
count_start_at.why: range 50 / 100 and band 50 / 100 are caps: most tracks and windows start below 20 or 50
count_start_at.closes: Y1.B6.S1: counting on from 20 to 50 only (the tracks and the chart start below 20); Y1.B12.S1: counting on from 50 to 100 only (the tracks and the chart deal mostly below 50)

tens_name_100.option: band: 100 (up to ten tens = 100); ask: the number (2 tens = 20) as well as how many tens
tens_name_100.name: Name the Tens to 100 (option)
tens_name_100.teaches: count the ten rods and write the number they make (20, 30 … 100), up to ten tens
tens_name_100.representation: the skill's own row of ten rods; one answer box for the number
tens_name_100.why: band 90 stops at 9 tens and the skill only asks "how many tens?"
tens_name_100.closes: Y1.B6.S2: saying and writing 20, 30, 40 and 50 for 2-5 tens (the skill answers only how many tens); Y1.B12.S2: counting the tens to 100, with 100 as ten tens (band 90 stops at 9 tens) and naming each multiple of ten

tens_ones_group.name: Count by Making Tens
tens_ones_group.teaches: counting a large set by circling groups of ten, then counting tens and ones
tens_ones_group.representation: a scattered set of 20-50 objects; circle tens, write ___ tens ___ ones = ___
tens_ones_group.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
tens_ones_group.closes: Y1.B6.S3: grouping a loose set into tens to count it

ruler_cm.name: Read a Centimetre Ruler (option)
ruler_cm.teaches: measuring lengths in whole centimetres, then millimetres, on a metric ruler (the skill reads inches only)
ruler_cm.representation: a unit option (cm, mm) on reading_ruler with the same arrow-and-ruler picture
ruler_cm.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

nonstandard_mass.name: Measure Mass with Cubes
nonstandard_mass.teaches: measuring mass with non-standard units (cubes, marbles) on a balance, and comparing masses by the count
nonstandard_mass.representation: a drawn balance with an object in one pan and cubes in the other; write how many cubes
nonstandard_mass.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
nonstandard_mass.closes: Y1.B8.S2: measuring mass with cubes on a balance; Y1.B8.S3: comparing two masses measured in cubes

capacity_early.name: Full, Empty, Holds More
capacity_early.teaches: capacity language (full, empty, half full, nearly full) and comparing how much two containers hold
capacity_early.representation: outline containers with a drawn fill line; circle full/empty or the one that holds more; option: order three
capacity_early.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
capacity_early.closes: Y1.B8.S4: full, empty, half full; Y1.B8.S5: comparing volume in containers

nonstandard_capacity.name: Measure Capacity with Cups
nonstandard_capacity.teaches: measuring capacity and volume with non-standard units (cups, spoons) and comparing
nonstandard_capacity.representation: containers with a count of cups drawn beside them; write how many cups; circle the one that holds more
nonstandard_capacity.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
nonstandard_capacity.closes: Y1.B8.S6: measuring capacity with cups or scoops; Y1.B8.S7: comparing capacities measured in cups

multiples_from_0.option: start at 0 (multiples only), band 20 / 50 / 100; the same on seq_5 and seq_10 (seq_10 gets band 100: it has only 50 and 1000)
multiples_from_0.name: Count in 2s, 5s, 10s from Zero (option)
multiples_from_0.teaches: count in 2s (or 5s, 10s) from 0 on true multiples and fill the next number, one count per page
multiples_from_0.representation: a number track of multiples with a picture strip (pairs of socks, hands, ten frames) above it
multiples_from_0.why: seq_2/5/10 deal 1, 3, 5 and 1, 11, 21; skip_count_line mixes 2s, 5s and 10s on one page
multiples_from_0.closes: Y1.B9.S1: counting in 2s from 0 on true multiples, a page of 2s alone, with pictured pairs; Y1.B9.S2: counting in 10s from 0 on true multiples to 100, a page of 10s alone; Y1.B9.S3: counting in 5s from 0 on true multiples, a page of 5s alone

equal_groups_early.name: Make Equal Groups
equal_groups_early.teaches: recognising, making and adding equal groups, and doubles as two equal groups
equal_groups_early.representation: groups drawn in rings; tick equal or not, write groups of and the repeated addition
equal_groups_early.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
equal_groups_early.closes: Y1.B9.S4: deciding whether groups are equal and saying equal / not equal

share_group.name: Share and Make Groups
share_group.teaches: sharing a small amount equally (one for you, one for me) and grouping into equal groups within 10, including odd amounts that do not share fairly
share_group.representation: counters drawn next to plates or rings; draw them shared or grouped; write how many each / how many groups; option: fair or not fair
share_group.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

halves_quarters_only.option: denoms: halves only / quarters only (also fraction_of_set)
halves_quarters_only.name: Halves Only / Quarters Only (option)
halves_quarters_only.teaches: shade a half (or a quarter) of a shape, or find a half (quarter) of a small set
halves_quarters_only.representation: the skill's own shape or set cell, denominator 2 or 4 alone
halves_quarters_only.why: the denominator family 2 also deals quarters and eighths
halves_quarters_only.closes: Y1.B10.S2: finding (shading) a half of a shape only; Y1.B10.S6: finding (shading) a quarter of a shape only; Y1.B10.S8: finding a quarter of a quantity only (the live option also deals halves and leaks thirds, fifths and sixths)

half_quarter.name: Halves and Quarters
half_quarter.teaches: finding and recognising a half and a quarter of a shape, an object and a small quantity (equal parts, 2 or 4)
half_quarter.representation: shapes and small sets of objects; shade or circle a half/quarter; tick if the parts are equal
half_quarter.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
half_quarter.closes: Y1.B10.S3: is this set in halves? (two equal groups or not); the live option leaks thirds, fifths and sixths; Y1.B10.S7: is this set in quarters? (four equal groups or not); the live option leaks thirds, fifths and sixths

turns.name: Whole, Half and Quarter Turns
turns.teaches: describing turns (whole, half, quarter, three-quarter; clockwise, anticlockwise) of an arrow or object
turns.representation: an arrow or object drawn before and after a turn; circle the turn from a word bank
turns.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
turns.closes: Y1.B11.S1: whole, half and quarter turns

position_map.name: Where Is It? Positions and Maps
position_map.teaches: position and direction language (on, under, next to, behind, in front, left, right, forwards, backwards), following and giving simple directions on a grid map
position_map.representation: a simple picture map on a square grid; answer where-is questions or follow arrows
position_map.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
position_map.closes: Y1.B11.S2: left and right; Y1.B11.S3: forwards and backwards moves

ordinal.name: 1st, 2nd, 3rd
ordinal.teaches: ordinal numbers (first to tenth) and their abbreviations for position in a line
ordinal.representation: a line of line-drawn children or objects with a start flag; circle the 3rd, write the position of the star
ordinal.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps

unitise_coins.name: One Coin, Many Ones (option)
unitise_coins.teaches: match one 5-cent or 10-cent coin to the same number of 1-cent coins
unitise_coins.representation: one coin on the left, rows of 1-cent coins on the right; circle the matching row
unitise_coins.why: coin_value finds coins by value; unitising is not dealt
unitise_coins.closes: Y1.B13.S1: unitising: one coin worth 5 or 10 is the same as 5 or 10 ones

money_notes.name: Recognise Notes (option)
money_notes.teaches: recognising banknotes and their values alongside coins (the school teaches US dollars)
money_notes.representation: add notes to the coin-value picture bank
money_notes.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
money_notes.closes: Y1.B13.S3: recognising bills and naming each bill's value

day_order.name: First, Next, Then
day_order.teaches: sequencing events and times of day (morning, afternoon, evening, night; before, after; first, next, then)
day_order.representation: three or four picture cards; number them 1-4 in order; option: before/after questions
day_order.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
day_order.closes: Y1.B14.S1: before and after; sequencing events

time_talk.name: Time Words
time_talk.teaches: the language of time (today, yesterday, tomorrow, days of the week, months, seasons, before, after)
time_talk.representation: calendar strip or picture timeline; circle or write the word from a bank
time_talk.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
time_talk.closes: Y1.B14.S2: days of the week in order; Y1.B14.S3: months of the year in order

time_units.name: Hours, Minutes or Seconds?
time_units.teaches: a sense of time units: which activities take seconds, minutes or hours
time_units.representation: activity pictures with a unit word bank; option: longer/shorter
time_units.why: existing WRM_PROPOSALS entry; covers these steps
time_units.closes: Y1.B14.S4: choosing hours, minutes or seconds for an activity
